text: Welcome to yet another episode of This is My Architecture.
I am Giriraj from AWS and today I have the pleasure to be joined by Pawan from Tata Global Beverages.
Welcome Pawan.
My pleasure.
Pawan, can you tell us what does Tata Global Beverages do?
Yeah, sure.
We are the second largest producer of tea and we have a significant play in coffee and water also.
Wow.
So tea coffee business and you migrated all in lock stock barrel to AWS.
I think that's what we are going to talk about today.
Can you get our viewers started by sharing how did you approach the migration of all your
enterprise applications to AWS?
Yeah, sure.
So, like any enterprise, the uptime is very important.
We cannot take extended down times just because we are doing a migration.
So, what we did was right at the start, the on-prem using a direct connect services, we
have connected it on AWS.
So, what it does is it gives us a seamless connectivity for all the on-prem workloads as well as users
to what we are new spinning up on the cloud.
Right after that, what we did was we started spinning up our workloads on AWS at EC2 level.
And what we ensured that we used the tested and tried method of doing the backups of the
databases, putting them onto S3s and then from there importing altogether new as a new instance
onto AWS.
Same time what we have done was we ensured that all the old operating systems and the databases
are taken care.
So, we have kind of set a standard, anything and everything which goes on AWS has to be
on the latest platform.
So, great.
So, you start with the network connectivity and then you build the entire application ground
up and as you said, you standardize the operating system as well.
So, that's another benefit of migration.
Interesting.
And any enterprise application migration journey, I think security remains your top priority.
So, how did you approach and implement security for your enterprise applications?
Yes.
So, what we have done is for our end users, we have kind of split our workload into Mumbai
into two zones, the AZs.
We have the load balancers coming in between.
And from there, if you see, we have Zscalers and Firewall WAF.
These are two specific purpose-built solution.
The Zscaler is especially for our end users.
What we do with Zscaler is, again, one of your partners, we build a user-to-application relationship.
So, user gets to see only what he's authorized to see.
He should not be able to see anything else.
The second thing is we have integrated it with our active directory on Azure, which helps
us inject the multi-factor authentication in between, right?
So, the workload which is for our end users is completely secured.
It is coming from a cloud broker.
Nobody else has the access.
We don't open any ports.
And it directly comes to our enterprise application.
Now, for our partners and customers, we use firewalls for all the B2B kind of relations.
We have a lot of orders comes from our modern trade partners.
And all of those workloads comes to our firewall.
From there, it goes to WAF.
And then, from there, it goes to our applications.
Very interesting.
So, users access the application and there is no network to user mapping.
Yes.
So, you don't enable access for users to the network.
And I think the rest of it is also coming along well.
So, how about GuardDuty?
How do you use GuardDuty in this architecture?
Well, something very interesting which we have done here is now GuardDuty is kind of another
service which is used from AWS.
It monitors all of our transactions at an infrastructure level which is happening on the infrastructure.
AWS VPC, yeah.
Yes.
And what it does is we filter down the critical alerts using Lambda.
And then, from here, we send it to a third party chat application as a group alerts.
So, ticketing was one method but this method alerts, sends us the alerts much faster than
anybody else can think of.
Wow.
So, now you are getting network issues alerts directly on your phone.
Yes.
So, we can then respond to it.
Yes.
This is a great way to secure and build a reliable application.
What is your perspective?
How did you manage cost while migrating all in on AWS?
Yeah.
Three specific things which we have done is when we are migrating, we ensure that we use lot
of managed services.
For an example, when we were on a data center, we had seven SMTP servers.
On AWS, we have just one and that also we use very less because we use the managed services
of SMTP.
Okay.
There are very few applications wherein we need to spin up an instance.
We had 300 servers, virtual servers on our data center.
On AWS, we have only 200 of them.
The second thing which we use is we are very serious about paper use.
We use a third party application ParkMyCloud which is integrated with AWS IAM services.
We have created the application server groups, map them to the application owners.
Now, they have the ability of spinning up their servers, start or shut down their own, right?
So infrastructure team doesn't come into picture.
There's no ticket.
They can do it themselves whenever they want it.
And the third thing which people, a lot of people don't realize is after moving to AWS,
our work has come down significantly on backup, on storage, on network.
So all of those work has gone out and we are getting the benefits on our managed services
contract.
In total, we are seeing roughly around 12 to 17 percent of total cost saving.
Wow, that's awesome.
And I am thinking with the self-service IT and the application owners getting a self-service
portal, they must be delighted with the kind of service they are getting from the IT team.
Yeah.
So great.
So what's from here?
What's next for you, Pawan, on AWS journey?
The very next thing is SAP HANA.
So we have started our discussion with AWS to move us on HANA.
So that's a big project for us.
We plan to simplify our business processes further and AWS is our chosen partner for that.
The second thing which we are doing is AI ML analytics.
So those are the solutions which we are going to use.
From an infrastructure perspective, we are going to further simplify our security with
the transit VPC and the shared VPC coming into picture.
If we see an opportunity by which we can simplify the way we have done the security today, we
can further simplify it.
Perfect.
Awesome.
This is very inspiring, Pawan.
I wish you good luck and wish you the best.
Thank you.
Thank you for sharing your story and spending time with us.
Thank you for watching yet another episode of This is My Architecture.
